title: Beef and Vegetables (Carrots, Broccoli, Dark‑Green Leafy Greens)

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of lean beef cubes combined with a mix of vegetables: carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens such as spinach, kale or Swiss chard. Beef provides a high‑quality source of protein, while the vegetables add vitamins, minerals and dietary fiber. The recipe is prepared without potatoes or gravy, making it low‑calorie and diet‑friendly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is an excellent source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant iron.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for its anti‑cancer properties.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens provide more calcium and magnesium than most other vegetables.
Traditional preparations steam or lightly sauté the ingredients in olive oil to preserve nutrients.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef supplies all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and carrots provide B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Broccoli and leafy greens are loaded with vitamin C, vitamin K and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The vegetables add fiber, promoting digestive health and satiety.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Choose lean cuts of beef; fatty cuts can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Vegetable allergies
items.content: Some individuals may react to broccoli or certain leafy greens.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Beef should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C (145 °F) to eliminate pathogens.

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should consume dark‑green greens in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main meal. Sear the beef cubes until browned, then simmer with carrots, broccoli and greens in a small amount of olive oil. Season with black pepper, garlic and rosemary if desired. Pair with whole‑grain couscous or quinoa for a complete plate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months after it has cooled completely.
